items.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: And so it was the Bill Potts Quartet. And we were a white band playing Harlem.

ctx.x: Okay. Bill Potts called me up. I was in the service. He was living in Washington. And he says, “I have a gig in Harlem, uptown.” At that time the whites and blacks could not mix at all. And that was 1947. And he says, “You want to come up and do it?” It was at night so I put on civilian clothes and I was playing six nights a week as a civilian and then go back to the base, which I don’t know if it was legal or illegal but I was doing it. And so it was the Bill Potts Quartet. And we were a white band playing…

Yeah. I was just going to ask, I wanted to know, in the Bill Potts Quartet and in this band with Keter, can you name a couple of the songs that would kind of summarize what you were doing at that point?
